sections.h2: Why is Oak Ridge a distinct place to sell a house?
sections.html:
Oak Ridge was built in 1942 as a Manhattan Project site, and it was incorporated as a city in 1959. The federal government bought nearly 60,000 acres of farmland in the Clinch River valley and laid out a planned town about 25 miles east of Knoxville. Many of the first houses were put up fast from cemesto panels, which are bonded cement and asbestos, so an inspector or buyer may ask about the original construction of an older house here.

The city sits across five parallel ridges and four valleys, with Melton Hill Lake on its northeast and east edges. The Census Bureau counts 85.25 square miles of land, and its July 1, 2025 estimate of 35,395 residents is 12.7% above the April 2020 base. Oak Ridge National Laboratory and the Y-12 complex remain major employers, and the school district's own news release mentions growth in the nuclear industry as a reason to plan for more students.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Oak Ridge homes?
sections.html:
The median owner-occupied home is valued at $270,200 for 2020 to 2024, and 65.8% of units are owner-lived. Median gross rent runs $1,131 a month. There are 14,015 households of 2.30 people on average, and 19.6% of residents are 65 or older, a higher share than the national 18.9%.

  • Median household income: $72,311
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 40.2%
  • Mean commute to work: 21.7 minutes
  • Residents in poverty: 12.2%

A large older population means many sellers are downsizing or settling an estate. See Census QuickFacts for Oak Ridge for the full list.

sections.h2: Does Oak Ridge send one tax bill or two?
sections.html:
Two. The city mails its own statement in July and collects it through the Utilities Business Office at 200 South Tulane Avenue, while the county portion is billed by Anderson or Roane County depending on where the parcel lies. About 16.25% of taxable real parcels are in the Roane County section. The city's published rate table shows the following.

Roane County (tax year 2022)$2.3136$2.34$4.6536

Residential property is assessed at 25%. On the Census median of $270,200, the assessed value is $67,550, and the city's share at $2.3136 works out to about $1,563. Rates after those years are not in the table, so ask the Utilities Business Office at (865) 425-3400 for the current figure. Source: the city's tax rate page.

sections.h2: When is Oak Ridge city tax due?
sections.html:
Owners have until August 31 to pay without interest, and interest starts accruing on September 1. Payment can be made online, at the Utilities Business Office, in its drop box or by mail to P.O. Box 1, Oak Ridge, TN 37831. Cards and online payments carry a 2.75% fee, and an eCheck costs $1 per $5,000.

The city mails notices to the owner address on file with the state as of January 1. If you sold in the spring or summer, the new owner may never see the bill, which is why the city says it is normally covered during closing. Missing a notice does not cancel the debt. Because the city bill falls due in summer and the county bill in the fall, a seller closing between the two should check both statements with the title company.

sections.h2: How recent is the last reappraisal for Oak Ridge properties?
sections.html:
The city reports that properties in both the Anderson and Roane sections were reappraised in fiscal years 2016 and 2021, tied to tax years 2015 and 2020. The city rate fell from $2.56 in the 2019 tax year to $2.3136 after that second reappraisal, a drop of about 10%, while the Anderson County rate fell from $2.6945 to $2.456.

Assessment ratios are fixed by state law at 25% for residential property, 40% for commercial and 30% for personal equipment. A seller who thinks the assessed value is too high should ask the county assessor, Anderson or Roane, for the review steps, because the city does not set the appraised value.

sections.h2: What property tax relief exists for Oak Ridge owners?
sections.html:
The state's tax freeze and relief programs work through the county. For tax year 2026, the Comptroller lists a freeze income limit of $53,900 for Anderson County and $43,460 for Roane County. Application deadlines fall 35 days after the local delinquency date.

If a seller already holds one of these benefits, the buyer's side should know before closing so that the numbers on the settlement statement match the bill actually due.

sections.h2: What local rules affect an Oak Ridge house sale?
sections.html:
Codes Enforcement, at 865-425-3532, issues all building permits and enforces the housing, plumbing, electrical and zoning codes. Permit work now runs through the CityView portal. The city also publishes a three-day appeal form for housing code violations, and it must be returned in person within three days of signing for a certified notice.

  • A vacant building must keep its doors and windows locked or otherwise secured.
  • Every house must show its number at the front entrance or on the mailbox.
  • A structure tax-delinquent for three years can be treated as deteriorated under the rental inspection chapter.

Chapter 5 of Title 13 lets the city set residential rental inspection districts, so a landlord selling a rental should ask Planning and Development whether the address falls in one. Investors buying as-is should expect these checks. See the city's Codes Enforcement page.

sections.h2: How does the recording process work for Oak Ridge sales?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded in the county that holds the parcel. Anderson County's Register of Deeds is at 100 North Main Street, Room 205, Clinton, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the office posts its indexes online without a user fee. Tennessee charges $0.37 per $100 of price on the transfer.

Before you order a title search, confirm whether your parcel is in Anderson or Roane County, since the two counties keep separate records and tax maps. A title company will normally handle both the search and the filing.

sections.h2: How are Oak Ridge schools and neighborhoods likely to figure in buyer questions?
sections.html:
Oak Ridge Schools reports 4,853 students in 2024 to 2025, a dip to 4,694 at the end of the next school year, and 4,795 enrolled by August 2026. Because the city runs its own district, buyers from out of town often ask whether a house falls within its zone, and the district can confirm that for a specific address.

Many homes sit on the steep northeastern slope of Blackoak Ridge, and the east-side lakefront has trails and picnic areas, so lot shape and slope matter more here than in a flat grid. Climate adds detail: the area averages about 59.7 inches of rain a year and 39 days at or above 90 degrees, so gutters, drainage and air conditioning are routine inspection items.

sections.h2: What are the fastest ways to sell an Oak Ridge house?
sections.html:
Listing with an agent suits a house in good shape that can wait for a buyer's financing. A cash offer fits a house that needs repairs, an inherited property or a rental with tenants. Closing then depends on clearing title and paying off any liens.

Get any offer in writing, ask who pays the recording tax, and have a title company confirm both the city and county tax status before closing.

faqs.q: When does Oak Ridge city property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: Interest starts on September 1. The city's statement arrives in July, and payment without penalty is allowed through August 31.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Oak Ridge deed?
faqs.a: The county where the parcel sits, Anderson or Roane. About 16.25% of taxable real parcels are in the Roane County section, so check your tax map first.

faqs.q: What is the Oak Ridge city tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's table lists $2.3136 per $100 of assessed value through the years shown. Ask the Utilities Business Office at (865) 425-3400 for the rate on your current bill.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to repair a house before selling it in Oak Ridge?
faqs.a: Yes for building work. Codes Enforcement issues all building permits and works with applicants who hold valid city or state trade licenses. Call 865-425-3532.

faqs.q: Can a buyer see my county records online?
faqs.a: Yes for Anderson County. Its Register of Deeds offers online access to indexes and images and has removed user fees.
